facts: Probe latencies in milliseconds: 92, 108, 97. The limit is 100 ms.
rule: Classify this canary deployment by a majority of probe results. A probe passes when latency is at most the documented limit. Return RELEASE only if at least two probes pass; otherwise return HOLD.
derivation: 92 and 97 pass; 108 fails. Two of three pass.

facts: Coverage by component: API 94 percent, worker 79 percent, gateway 96 percent. Required component minimum: 80 percent.
rule: Assess the coverage floor independently for every component, without averaging. Choose READY only when each component meets its minimum; choose GAP when even one component is below it.
derivation: Worker coverage 79 is below 80 despite the high average.

facts: Inspected records: 200. Invalid records: 6. The maximum accepted invalid fraction is 2 percent.
rule: Determine whether the invalid-record fraction exceeds the acceptance budget. Divide invalid by inspected; an exact equality is accepted. The decision labels are ACCEPT for a fraction within budget and REJECT for a fraction above it.
derivation: 6/200 is 3 percent, exceeding 2 percent.

facts: Rollback rehearsal: passed. Backup restoration: failed. Availability probe: passed.
rule: Authorize a cutover only when both rollback rehearsal and backup restoration have passed. Availability is informational and cannot substitute for either safety check. Choose GO if both mandatory checks passed, otherwise WAIT.
derivation: Backup restoration failed, so the conjunction is false.

facts: Current queue depth: 75. Last state: ACTIVE. Enter ACTIVE above 90; leave ACTIVE below 60.
rule: Apply the documented hysteresis transitions to the last state. Inside the band, including either boundary, preserve the last state. Choose the resulting state ACTIVE or IDLE; do not classify using a single midpoint threshold.
derivation: 75 is between 60 and 90, so the previous ACTIVE state remains.

facts: Required artifacts: manifest, license, checksum. Uploaded artifacts: manifest, checksum, readme.
rule: Compute the required artifacts absent from the uploaded set. Ignore uploaded extras. If exactly license is missing choose LICENSE; if nothing is missing choose COMPLETE; otherwise choose OTHER.
derivation: Required minus uploaded contains only license.

facts: Security reviewers: Inez, Omar. Operations reviewers: Omar, Pia. Privacy reviewers: Omar, Inez.
rule: Find a reviewer present in all three reviewer sets. Use NONE if their intersection is empty and MULTIPLE if it contains more than one name; otherwise use the single uppercase name from OMAR or INEZ.
derivation: Omar is the only member common to all three sets.

facts: Previous active services: cedar, elm, fir. Current active services: elm, fir, pine.
rule: Identify services retired between snapshots: present previously and absent currently. Newly introduced services are not retirements. Choose CEDAR if it is the sole retirement, PINE if it is the sole retirement, and OTHER for any other retired set.
derivation: Previous minus current is cedar; pine is an addition.

facts: Desired replicas: east, north. Observed replicas: north, west.
rule: Measure configuration drift using the symmetric difference, counting each location missing from either side once. Select ZERO, ONE, or TWO according to that count. Shared locations contribute nothing.
derivation: east is missing and west is extra; north matches.

facts: Approval events: Ada approve; Ada approve; Bo approve; Cy reject. Required distinct approving people: 3.
rule: Deduplicate approving people before applying the approval quorum. Duplicate events from one person never add a vote, and rejection is not approval. Choose QUORUM for at least three distinct approving people and SHORT otherwise.
derivation: Only Ada and Bo approve; there are two distinct approvals.

facts: Job requires 7 slots. Free slots: amber 6, blue 9, coral 12.
rule: Place the job in the feasible pool with the smallest free capacity, to minimize unused slots after placement. Feasible means its free slots cover the entire job. Choose AMBER, BLUE, CORAL, or NONE if none fits.
derivation: Blue and coral fit; blue has the smaller capacity.

facts: Free capacity is 10 units. An indivisible batch contains jobs requiring 4, 4, and 3 units.
rule: Admit this batch only if every job fits together. Jobs cannot be split and partial admission is forbidden. Choose ADMIT when the sum fits the available capacity and DEFER otherwise.
derivation: 4+4+3=11, exceeding the free capacity of 10.

facts: Pool A has 12 free slots and reserve 6. Pool B has 10 free slots and reserve 2. Job size is 7.
rule: Subtract each pool's mandatory reserve before testing whether the job fits. Choose A or B if exactly one is eligible, BOTH if both are eligible, or NONE. Reserves may not be consumed by the job.
derivation: Usable A=6, B=8; only B can accommodate seven.

facts: Available budget: 8. Jobs in priority order: first costs 6, second costs 5, third costs 2.
rule: Scan the jobs once in their documented priority order. Accept a job if it fits the remaining budget, otherwise skip it and continue. Choose FIRST_THIRD for that accepted pair, FIRST_ONLY for only first, and OTHER otherwise.
derivation: Accept six, skip five with two remaining, then accept two.

facts: Existing replicas: zone A=2, zone B=1, zone C=1. Eligible zones: A, B, C.
rule: Assign one new replica to the eligible zone with the fewest existing replicas. Break equal counts by alphabetically earliest zone name. Choose A, B, or C; total cluster capacity is not the selection criterion.
derivation: B and C tie at one replica; B sorts first.

facts: Reservation A: [09:00,10:00). Reservation B: [10:00,11:00). Both are UTC on the same day.
rule: Decide whether these half-open reservations overlap. Their start is included and end excluded. Choose CLASH for any shared instant and CLEAR otherwise. Touching at an excluded end is not overlap.
derivation: A excludes 10:00, the first instant included by B.

facts: Authorization expires at 14:30 UTC. Evaluation time is exactly 14:30 UTC on the same date.
rule: An authorization is usable strictly before its expiry and invalid at or after it. Compare the two times without adding a grace period. Choose VALID or EXPIRED according to this boundary rule.
derivation: Evaluation equals expiry, which is outside the valid interval.

facts: Local maintenance start: 18:00 at fixed offset UTC+02:00. Required UTC window: [15:30,16:30].
rule: Convert the local start to UTC by subtracting its fixed offset, then test the inclusive UTC window. Choose INSIDE if the converted time lies in that window and OUTSIDE otherwise. There is no daylight-saving adjustment.
derivation: 18:00 minus two hours is 16:00 UTC, within the stated window.

facts: Incident opened at 09:10 UTC and acknowledged at 09:27 UTC, same date. Acknowledgement SLA: at most 15 minutes.
rule: Classify acknowledgement timeliness using elapsed minutes from opening. Exactly the SLA limit is on time. Choose ON_TIME when the duration is within limit, otherwise LATE; compare duration rather than clock-hour equality.
derivation: Elapsed time is 17 minutes, two beyond the limit.

facts: The last checkpoint was day 12. Checkpoints are due every 7 days thereafter. Current day: 26.
rule: A checkpoint is due when the number of days since the last checkpoint is a positive multiple of the interval. Choose DUE or NOT_DUE. Treat days as integer sequence positions rather than dates with weekends.
derivation: 26-12=14, a positive multiple of seven.

facts: Publish requires package. Package requires scan. Scan is blocked. Publish and package are not independently blocked.
rule: Determine readiness for Publish by following all prerequisite edges transitively. Any blocked prerequisite prevents readiness, even if the immediate prerequisite has no local block. Choose READY or BLOCKED.
derivation: Publish depends on package, which depends on the blocked scan.

facts: Gate states: build passed, smoke passed, performance failed. Mandatory gates: build, smoke. Performance is advisory.
rule: Evaluate only the mandatory gate set for launch admission. An advisory failure must be recorded but does not veto admission. Choose ALLOW if every mandatory gate passes; otherwise choose BLOCK.
derivation: Both mandatory gates passed; the failing gate is advisory.

facts: Healthy members: n1 in east, n2 in east, n3 in west. Failed member: n4 in south. Required healthy failure domains: 3.
rule: Assess quorum by distinct failure domains represented by healthy members, not by member count. Failed members contribute no domain. Choose MET for at least three healthy domains and UNMET otherwise.
derivation: The three healthy nodes span only east and west.

facts: Routes in preference order: primary unavailable; warm degraded; cold healthy. Degraded routes are ineligible.
rule: Select the first eligible route in preference order. Only healthy routes are eligible; do not stop at a degraded route. Choose PRIMARY, WARM, COLD, or NONE when no route qualifies.
derivation: Primary and warm are ineligible; cold is the first healthy route.

facts: Writer roles: east active, west active, north standby. Required active writer count: exactly one.
rule: Check the exclusive-writer invariant. Choose HEALTHY for exactly one active writer, SPLIT for more than one, and EMPTY for none. Standby writers do not count as active.
derivation: There are two active writers, east and west.

facts: Ownership map: / => core; /api => services; /api/auth => identity. Requested path: /api/auth/login.
rule: Resolve ownership by the longest matching path prefix, with slash-separated path components. A more specific matching prefix overrides a broader one. Choose CORE, SERVICES, or IDENTITY.
derivation: /api/auth is the longest matching ownership prefix.

facts: Original owner: Lina. Delegate: Miro. Delegation valid from day 5 through day 9 inclusive. Current day: 10.
rule: Use the delegate only during the inclusive delegation interval; outside it responsibility returns to the original owner. Select LINA or MIRO for today's owner. A previously valid delegation is not permanent.
derivation: Day 10 is beyond day 9, so Lina owns the work again.

facts: Rotation order: Ada, Bo, Cy. Ada owns cycle 0. Requested cycle: 5.
rule: Advance one position per cycle in the repeating roster, wrapping after its last member. Use zero-based cycle numbering as specified. Choose ADA, BO, or CY for the requested cycle.
derivation: 5 modulo 3 equals 2, which is Cy's position.

facts: Rules: all regions => global; EU => europe; EU plus regulated data => compliance. Request: EU, regulated data.
rule: Choose the owner attached to the matching rule with the most conditions. The region-and-data rule is more specific than region alone, which is more specific than the default. Choose GLOBAL, EUROPE, or COMPLIANCE.
derivation: Both EU and regulated conditions match the most specific rule.

facts: Eligible owners and priority: team A=4, team B=4, team C=2. Higher priority is preferred.
rule: Assign directly only if exactly one eligible owner has maximal priority. A tie at the maximum requires escalation rather than an alphabetical choice. Choose A, B, C, or ESCALATE.
derivation: A and B tie for highest priority, so assignment must escalate.

facts: Opening inventory: 25. Receipts: 9. Dispatches: 7. Recorded closing inventory: 27.
rule: Compute expected closing inventory as opening plus receipts minus dispatches. Compare it with the recorded close. Choose MATCH if equal, SHORT if recorded is lower, and EXCESS if recorded is higher.
derivation: 25+9-7=27, matching the recorded close.

facts: Batch A: 10 requests, 2 errors. Batch B: 90 requests, 0 errors. Allowed pooled error rate: at most 3 percent.
rule: Evaluate the pooled error rate from total errors divided by total requests. Do not average the two batch percentages. Choose WITHIN for a pooled rate within the allowed maximum and OVER otherwise.
derivation: 2/100 is 2 percent, within 3; the unweighted average would be wrong.

facts: Artifact size: 1536 MiB. Available allocation: 2 GiB. Binary conversion: 1 GiB = 1024 MiB.
rule: Convert available allocation into the same unit as artifact size before comparing. Select FIT if the artifact does not exceed allocation and TOO_LARGE otherwise. Use the documented binary conversion, not a decimal multiplier.
derivation: 2 GiB equals 2048 MiB; 1536 fits.

facts: Meter revision 1 reports 18 units. Revision 2 explicitly replaces revision 1 and reports 21 units. Allowed limit: 20.
rule: A replacement revision supersedes the earlier measurement; revisions are not additive and must not be averaged. Compare the latest replacement value to the inclusive limit. Choose UNDER_LIMIT or OVER_LIMIT.
derivation: The current reading is 21, above the inclusive limit 20.

facts: Expected sensor value: 100. Observed value: 97. Allowed absolute deviation: 3.
rule: Compute the absolute difference between observed and expected values. Equality with the allowed deviation is acceptable. Choose IN_TOLERANCE or OUT_OF_TOLERANCE; do not use a signed difference or a percentage tolerance.
derivation: Absolute difference is 3, exactly the accepted boundary.

facts: General policy: archive completed cases. Named legal-hold exceptions: case-17. Current case: case-17, completed.
rule: Apply named legal-hold exceptions before the general archive rule. A case on hold must be retained even when completed. Choose RETAIN or ARCHIVE for this case.
derivation: case-17 is specifically held; the exception overrides completion.

facts: Candidate A: severity 2, age 90. Candidate B: severity 3, age 10. Candidate C: severity 3, age 30. Higher severity is more urgent; higher age is older.
rule: Choose the next incident lexicographically: maximize severity first, then age among tied-severity incidents. Never let age override a higher severity. Choose A, B, or C.
derivation: B and C have maximal severity; C is older.

facts: Role permits export. Resource grant permits export. An explicit current revocation prohibits export.
rule: Resolve these policy records using deny-overrides semantics: any explicit current revocation wins over every permit. Choose PERMIT or DENY. The number of permits does not outweigh revocation.
derivation: The explicit current revocation overrides both permit records.

facts: Required fields: checksum, license. Checksum is verified. License status is unknown, not explicitly invalid.
rule: Use three-valued readiness: any known-invalid required field yields REJECT; otherwise any unknown required field yields REVIEW; otherwise choose ACCEPT. Unknown is neither verified nor known-invalid.
derivation: No known invalid field exists, but the license remains unknown.

facts: Unsigned note at revision 9 names BLUE. Signed policy at revision 4 names GREEN. Both concern the same routing choice.
rule: Select the routing value from the highest-authority record: signed policy outranks an unsigned note. Use recency only to break ties within the same authority class. Choose BLUE or GREEN.
derivation: The signed policy outranks the newer unsigned note.
